canonical_definition:
What it is. Across the available definitions, ETHOS is treated as a dataset for detecting hate speech. The only description provided places it in binary classification experiments where papers report F1 score under optimized prompts.

What it is claimed to measure. Papers do not link ETHOS to any construct or behavioral indicator. In the available usage, it is reported as an evaluation dataset for F1 score in hate speech detection, rather than being tied to a broader set of measurement claims.

Space of uses. The available paper uses ETHOS alongside ArSarcasm, Liar, and BBH-navigate, reporting F1 score across these benchmarks. In that usage, ETHOS appears as one item in a multi-dataset evaluation setup for prompt optimization.
papers: Efficient and Accurate Prompt Optimization: the Benefit of Memory in Exemplar-Guided Reflection
Interpret and Improve In-Context Learning via the Lens of Input-Label Mappings
SEE: Strategic Exploration and Exploitation for Cohesive In-Context Prompt Optimization
